claims.text: The initial equiatomic FeCoNi-based alloy is fcc, has high saturation magnetization, and has low coercivity.
Adding Mn produces an equiatomic FeCoNiMn alloy.
Equiatomic FeCoNiMn has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
High-temperature processing followed by rapid thermal annealing can produce a single-phase fcc or slightly distorted FeCoNiMn structure.
Post-synthesis heat treatment will maximize FeCoNiMn homogeneity and promote beneficial microstructural ordering.
Mn substitution introduces local lattice distortion and ordering in FeCoNiMn.
The Mn-induced structural changes enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Mn-induced strain fields act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Mn substitution alters electronic and magnetic interactions in the FeCoNi matrix and thereby increases intrinsic anisotropy.
Enhanced anisotropy and substitution-induced strain create barriers to domain-wall motion.
Barriers to domain-wall motion increase coercivity.
FeCoNiMn will have higher coercivity than FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
FeCoNiMn will largely retain the high saturation magnetization of the FeCoNi-based baseline.
Previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys are soft ferromagnets with low coercivity.
The coercivity-enhancing effect should apply while FeCoNiMn remains near-equiatomic and high in configurational entropy.
Excess Mn or departure from equiatomic balance could cause phase separation or a marked loss of saturation magnetization.
Rapid thermal annealing causes a large coercivity increase in fcc FeCoNiMnCu films through microstructural changes, strain-induced anisotropy enhancement, and stronger domain-wall pinning.
High cubic symmetry limits intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy, whereas low-symmetry ordering and strong spin-orbit coupling favor strong anisotropy.

contradictions.description: Mn is described as a minor substitution, but equiatomic quaternary FeCoNiMn contains 25 at.% Mn, which is not ordinarily a minor fraction.

The intervention specifies a fixed equiatomic FeCoNiMn composition, while the experiment proposes a series of equiatomic alloys with varying Mn substitution levels; varying Mn content is incompatible with keeping all four components equiatomic.
